title: Using mlflow to compare service (custom-RAG & fetch), temperature & model combinations with godot + kit
author: bigorangemachine
selftext:
After a bunch of effort I finally got a steady test run in.

Lots of confusing little mistakes.

I didn't have a `.mcpignore` so the agent wandered around my project directory find a better example of the prompt to use.  I was really confused why the first couple of runs had the same token usage within a couple hundred which seemed weird.  What's also weird is that the larger the context somehow made the unit tests fail so trying to scale into larger features will lead to obvious mistakes

I setup about a 6 model configurations and 3 mcp configurations.  I built a RAG chroma-db based on the godot documentation 

I haven't tested each iteration yet but I did notice some failed tool calls that weren't being tracked.  This dataset implies that system prompts and temperature don't matter but the un-tweaked models are just having all sorts of failures.

So far the combination I know that generally makes the best result has the highest token usage.  But for sure the lower token users, lower service users and lower run times are definitely suffering from silent untracked failures

What I see so far is that in the system prompt I'm encouraging it to do a subagent code review which isn't happening.  I did a test just calling a subagent and it show up in the metrics but for whatever reason neither model is not calling the subagent.

What is neat about mlflow is that it's just a data collector.  So you can setup whatever pipeline you want and you got ways to collect data.  I originally was going to compare another mcp-go-lang host but I eventually ran down that the mcp-host I originally tried was swaping tabs for spaces which is a non-starter in godot.  Once I saw it was an issue I didn't look back.

Now I objectively have a way to test & measure local models.  I can determine if a RAG service is worth it... or just fetch is fine... Another interesting insight is that trying to self-compact a system prompt with lower temperature resulted in more tool calls; there is a benefit to being more descriptive and opening up more creativity/temperature to get better outcomes

So far I just tried Qwen3:30b & Gemma4:26b but haven't manually tested Qwen yet.  What I'm really interested in is if the pipeline could accommodate RL e2e tests & update those tests.  I used gemini to suggest parameters that were equivalent between the two using similar goals.  Surprisingly a slightly more creative (higher temperature) model seems to be better but my insights are anecdotal for now.  I tried with Claude as well and it was able to achieve the goal pretty good but needed some follow up prompts the open models handled better in a one-shot.

I was hoping to have something to share on github soon but as I was refining and expanding the test suite I had more bugs etc.  I'm just happy to finally have a full test run successful and got all my scripts working together properly finally... but I'm happy to finally have a way to test iterations of system prompts and prompts using a template based approach.
